title: Framed envelope protocol + resumable tool invocation patterns for polyglot SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a small framing/envelope protocol and resumable session pattern to unify streaming tool/function calling and structured outputs across TypeScript/Python/Go SDKs. Goal: make SDKs interoperable with incremental outputs, allow client-side rehydration of partially-completed tool invocations, and provide clear typed envelopes that survive network reconnects and language boundary differences.
decision_notes: Use length-prefixed JSON 'envelopes' with a stable 'envelope_type' field (event, tool_call, tool_output, checkpoint, error) so non-blocking receivers can parse partial streams deterministically.
Adopt a resumable session token returned by the runtime for long-running tool invocations. Session token can be used to request missed envelopes via an incremental fetch API.
Keep envelope payloads small and prefer references (KV cache key / blob id) for large binary outputs. SDKs will provide helper utilities for streaming those referenced blobs.
Backwards compatibility: runtime will still respond with plain streaming text for simple generation endpoints. Framed envelopes are opt-in via `envelope: framed` param on the request.
Expose ergonomic helper classes in each SDK to hide framing details and provide typed events (ProgressEvent, ToolCallEvent, StructuredOutputEvent, CheckpointEvent, ErrorEvent).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime supports `envelope: framed` param and returns length-prefixed JSON envelopes over existing streaming socket and HTTP chunking paths.
TypeScript SDK exposes FramedStreamReader and async iterator helpers that yield typed envelope objects with TypeScript types for tool calls and structured outputs.
Python SDK exposes an async generator `stream_envelopes()` that yields dict envelopes and provides `resume(session_token)` helper to fetch missing envelopes.
Go SDK exposes a channel-based EnvelopeStreamer with a `Resume(sessionToken)` method and a small example demonstrating incremental tool rehydration.
Integration e2e test that simulates network interruption and uses session token to resume and reconstruct a tool invocation result.
Documentation page and migration guide published in Confluence/Docs with examples for each language.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): add envelope framing support to runtime behind `envelope=framed` flag. Ship TypeScript helper library only. Collect telemetry about envelope sizes and session token churn.
Phase 2: implement Python/Go helpers and sample apps. Publish SDK minor versions with docs. Run compatibility tests against existing production workloads (no default opt-in).

Phase 3: enable framed envelopes for selected public models that produce structured outputs (reranking, tools) and announce migration path for customers. Provide step-by-step examples to switch from text streaming to framed envelopes.
Phase 4: deprecate legacy internal-only streaming variants after 3 months of stable telemetry and migration completion support.
test_plan: Unit tests for FramedStreamReader parsing boundary conditions (split JSON across chunks, incorrect length header, extra bytes after envelope).
Integration test: simulated connection drop at seq N, resume with session_token and verify sequences N+1..end are returned and re-applied to client state machine.
Load test: measure per-envelope overhead at 5000 concurrent streams and ensure 99th percentile additional latency per token < 2ms.
Fuzz test: random length header corruption and ensure client fails gracefully and exposes a helpful error event for operator tooling.
rollout_plan: Week 1: runtime canary with envelope=framed on staging. TS SDK alpha published to npm tagged as `framed-alpha`.
Week 2: internal dogfood — platform team integrates framed envelopes into the console log ingestion path for structured events.
Week 3: publish Python/Go examples and a migration doc. Open early access for a handful of customers (enterprise) to try resumable tool calls.
Week 4: widen availability, flip feature flag for more models, monitor errors and session token replays. Postmortem and final tweaks before general availability.
risks: Increased wire overhead for many small envelopes may increase costs for high QPS workloads. Mitigation: coalescing small events at runtime and advising batch/aggregate patterns in docs.
Customers building custom parsers may mis-handle partial frames and produce silent failures. Mitigation: provide robust SDK helpers and a small 'framed-stream-validator' utility binary.
Session token proliferation could add state to runtime. Mitigation: TTLs and optional client-side checkpointing to reduce server-side retention.
Potential developer confusion with two streaming modes (legacy vs framed). Mitigation: clear docs, examples, and migration checklist.
